content.text: No restrictive covenant exists anywhere in the agreement; the capacity provisions are freedom-preserving and mutual.

input.quote: 12.22 Notwithstanding any other provisions in this Paragraph 12, when the Equipped Capacity is expanded to six (6) times of Initial Equipped Capacity or three (3) years after the RFS date whichever comes first, any Party is entitled to make available any of its Allocated Capacity for use by other Carriers on any commercial basis without any restrictions.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding us. Searches for "compete/competing" return only "competent jurisdiction/tribunal" (p0272, p0275), and there is no "shall not develop/market/sell", exclusivity, territory or competing-products covenant anywhere. The capacity provisions in Paragraph 12 are asset-governance rules applying mutually to every Party, and they are freedom-preserving in our favour: Subparagraph 12.20 entitles any Party to sell IRU from its Allocated Capacity "without any restrictions", 12.22 permits making Allocated Capacity available to other Carriers "on any commercial basis without any restrictions", and 12.7 expressly allows a Party to interconnect its WAC "with other communication systems". Paragraph 17.4 likewise bars Terminal Parties from impeding Direct Access. Carrier-status and use conditions (12.1, 12.6, 12.13-12.15) limit how consortium capacity may be used and transferred rather than what business we may operate or what products we may buy or build, they bind all Parties equally, and 12.15 requires them to be relaxed over time; they therefore do not engage this rule. The clause set meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.
